title: Analyze AeroSpace as an alternative for spaces
description:
AeroSpace (https://github.com/nikitabobko/AeroSpace) is another window manager for macOS. Analyze it as an alternative to yabai and to upstream hs.spaces (pull request #371), using the same questions this epic has asked of yabai. Check the following, and verify each from its documentation or source rather than from memory:

1. What AeroSpace's workspaces are. Find out whether they are macOS Spaces or its own, and what that means for Mission Control and for other applications.
2. Whether it needs System Integrity Protection disabled, and which permissions it needs.
3. How a client talks to it. Find out whether it has a socket, what the protocol is, and whether a client can receive events without running a shell command for each one.
4. How it names workspaces, and whether names survive a restart. This matters because the Spoon identifies spaces by name.
5. Which of the functions in hs_yabai-gt/ai/hs1-spaces.org and the adopted features in yabai-extras.org it provides.
6. Its license, how it is maintained, and whether it works on macOS 27.
7. Whether it can be used without tiling, since tiling was left out of this epic.

Write the analysis in hs_yabai-gt/ai, and end it with a comparison of yabai, AeroSpace and hs.spaces from #371. Do not install AeroSpace without asking the user first.
acceptance_criteria: The analysis answers all seven questions with sources, and ends with the comparison. The user has approved closing this bead.
notes: Analysis in hs_yabai-gt/ai/aerospace.org, from the clone at ~/git.w/AeroSpace (commit 6ed6af62). AeroSpace emulates workspaces by moving hidden windows off-screen instead of using macOS Spaces; needs no SIP; its socket keeps connections open, has a documented protocol and a subscribe command that streams events as JSON; workspace names persist in its config. Not installed or tested.
close_reason: Analysis in hs_yabai-gt/ai/aerospace.org; AeroSpace rejected because it replaces macOS Spaces; approved by user

title: Record findings on yabai's socket, its license, and upstream hs.spaces
description:
While discussing the evaluation in eqg.3, several findings came up that change the direction of the epic. Record them in hs_yabai-gt/ai:

1. yabai's socket answers one request per connection and never writes to a client, so events reach a client only through a shell command run by a signal. A measurement showed that a request over the socket costs far less than running yabai -m as a process.
2. yabai and Hammerspoon 2 are both under the MIT license.
3. Hammerspoon 2 already has hs.socket, which supports Unix domain sockets, and hs.window already uses a private SkyLight function.
4. Upstream Hammerspoon 2 has an open pull request, #371, that ports hs.spaces from Hammerspoon 1 without needing SIP disabled, and an issue, #86, about switching spaces with synthesized swipes. The pull request lacks moving a window to a space and instant switching, both of which yabai has.
acceptance_criteria: The findings are written up in hs_yabai-gt/ai with their sources. The user has approved closing this bead.
notes: Written: the socket's one-request behaviour, the cost measurement and the events section in hs_yabai-gt/ai/yabai.org; the licenses, hs.socket, PR #371 and issue #86 in hs_yabai-gt/ai/upstream-hs-spaces.org. Question 1 of eqg.3 is answered there: hs.socket supports Unix domain sockets.
close_reason: Findings in hs_yabai-gt/ai/yabai.org and upstream-hs-spaces.org; approved by user

title: Evaluate whether a Spoon can talk to yabai over its socket
description:
Inspect yabai's architecture and decide whether a Hammerspoon 2 Spoon can use it through its Unix socket instead of its command line. Start from hs_yabai-gt/ai/yabai.org, which already records the socket path and the format of requests and replies. The report must answer these questions:

1. Can Hammerspoon 2 open a Unix socket? If it cannot, the limitation is in Hammerspoon 2 and is a candidate for an upstream issue. Calling the yabai command line instead would start a process for every call.
2. Which commands fail without the scripting addition? System Integrity Protection stays enabled, so the scripting addition is not loaded. Test this rather than relying on the fork's readme.
3. How can space change events reach Hammerspoon 2? yabai reports events by running a shell command registered as a signal. Find something that Hammerspoon 2 can receive directly, and avoid polling.
4. Do yabai's window identifiers match those of HSWindow?

The Spoon's name is already decided: hs_yabai-gt. The report ends with a recommendation to go ahead or to stop, and a list of the beads that the implementation needs, if those differ from the ones already filed. Record what is learned in hs_yabai-gt/ai/yabai.org.
acceptance_criteria: A written report answering all five questions. The user has approved the decision to go ahead or to stop.
notes:
The inventory in hs_yabai-gt/ai/hs1-spaces.org adds questions for this evaluation. The Spoon names spaces with yabai labels, so the report must also answer: how the Spoon learns that yabai restarted, so it can apply the labels again; and how each name is matched to its space after macOS restarts. See the open questions at the end of that file.

notes:
Inventory written to hs_yabai-gt/ai/hs1-spaces.org: every public function of hs.spaces and the watcher, with the yabai command for each. Main findings: yabai selects spaces by index or label, not by ID; space --create and --destroy need SIP disabled, while Hammerspoon 1 adds and removes spaces through Mission Control with no SIP change; window --space does not need the scripting addition according to src/space_manager.c; screensHaveSeparateSpaces and missionControlSpaceNames have no yabai equivalent.

Decided on 2026-11-14: the Spoon's configuration maps names to positions, and the Spoon applies the labels from it. Open: whether a position is yabai's global index or a display plus a place on it.

title: install yabai
description:
Install the yabai fork for macOS 27 from https://github.com/Christian-SC26/yabai/releases.

Record the installed version and how it was installed. Find out whether its scripting addition is needed, and whether loading it requires System Integrity Protection to be partly disabled on macOS 27. Record which steps needed a human, so that the Spoon's readme can describe the setup.
acceptance_criteria: yabai runs and answers a query over its socket. The user has approved closing this bead.
notes:
Installed yabai-v7.3.3 on 2026-11-14 with: brew install christian-sc26/formulae/yabai (binary /opt/homebrew/Cellar/yabai/7.3.3/bin/yabai, linked as /opt/homebrew/bin/yabai). macOS 27.0.1, arm64.

The user decided not to modify SIP, so the scripting addition is not loaded. The fork's readme says space focus works without it; moving spaces and changing window layers need it.

Started with yabai --start-service, which installed ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.asmvik.yabai.plist. No yabairc exists, so the layout is float. The daemon aborted with 'could not access accessibility features', so the Accessibility grant has to be given by hand. Each brew upgrade installs a new versioned path, and macOS asks for Accessibility again.
After the user granted Accessibility by hand, yabai --restart-service started the daemon and created /tmp/yabai_$USER.socket (mode srw-------). yabai -m query --spaces returned the three spaces on three displays. A request written straight to the socket from Python, without the yabai command line, also worked: a little-endian int32 length, then each argument followed by a NUL byte, then one more NUL. The reply was JSON, and the daemon closed the connection after it. The warning 'could not locate config file' only means there is no yabairc.
The installation, the socket protocol, and the stop and removal commands are written up in hs_yabai-gt/ai/yabai.org.
close_reason: Installed yabai-v7.3.3 without the scripting addition; socket verified; documented in hs_yabai-gt/ai/yabai.org; approved by user

title: Spaces support for Hammerspoon 2 through yabai
description:
Hammerspoon 2 has no way to inspect or control macOS Spaces. The yabai fork for macOS 27 (https://github.com/Christian-SC26/yabai/releases) can control Spaces and accepts commands over a Unix socket.

This epic evaluates whether a Spoon can talk to yabai over that socket, without calling the yabai command line. If the evaluation is positive, it implements that Spoon and gives Hammerspoon 2 commands for Spaces. The target is at least the functionality of hs.spaces in Hammerspoon 1, whose source is in ~/git.w/hammerspoon/extensions/spaces, plus any yabai features worth adopting.
